academicJudgment.positive: Six taught economics courses span micro/macro/public/behavioural analysis and econometrics. Accounting, banking, firms and empirical research provide sustained business/economic inquiry. This establishes target responsiveness beyond general coherence.
academicJudgment.limitations: No dedicated development/labour/history-of-economics sequence, full corporate-finance pathway, two-stage econometrics or required economics thesis. Political, social and environmental courses are specific complements, not substitutes.
academicJudgment.adverseTest: Requiring additional named preparation would change formal eligibility but would not eliminate the verified subject core. The claim explicitly excludes an eligible external progression pathway.

interestReview.ownership: Rows 1992/1993/1994/1998/2001 are covered by the core; 1989/1990/1997 generate responsible-policy study; 1991/1996/2000 finance and 1995/1999 accounting are individually assessed rejected specialist directions. No search-only row generates an option. All 41 current exact-target rows retained and checked.

courseReview.evidenceBoundary: Actual profiles/methods where present, description2 for description-only courses. No enrichment is invented. Climate impacts, planetary constraints, lifecycle costs, political institutions and inequality have specific complementary policy roles. PPD is mandatory.

candidateReview.distinctness: Banking, mathematical statistics, consumer marketing and organizational behaviour yield to commercial law, international politics, planetary foundations and social/environmental justice. These five substitutions change priorities rather than labels.

rejected.label: Finance and financial market stability
rejected.reason: Money, Banking & Finance supplies asset pricing, risk, regulation and a bank simulation; Accounting adds investment appraisal. Both are already in the closest programme. These real contributions do not supply a sustained distinct 24-course finance route with further specialist investment and risk study.

rejected.label: Accounting and financial reporting
rejected.reason: The current UCR workbook has one accounting and corporate finance course but no advanced financial reporting, management accounting, auditing or control sequence to anchor a separate 24-course accounting route.

stopping.assessment: The closest UCR response retains economic theory, finance, business and quantitative research. The second route shifts five substantive courses toward economic policy, responsible firms and sustainability. Both remain feasible and differ by five courses each. Separate specialist finance and accounting routes are evidenced but cannot form credible distinct 24-course programmes from the current UCR offer without weak substitutes.

alignmentReview.finding: Economic theory, statistical/econometric methods, accounting, marketing, strategy and trade have identified primary-content relationships. Dedicated later methods, labour/development economics, game theory, economic history, financial policy and thesis retain gaps. The single taught econometrics course is not duplicated across both external stages; optional research is outside 180 EC.
alignmentReview.externalChoice: 24 EC is approved choice; no unrestricted guarantee, extra elective entitlement or missing content is inferred.

sourceFirstChallenge.reviewerOrPass: Stage 2 source-first second pass by the same AI
sourceFirstChallenge.independenceLimit: No independent human or separate-agent review. The second pass re-established the claim from the OER and current workbook, then challenged the finished pair.
sourceFirstChallenge.externalStartingPoint: Actual printed OER pp.34–36 confirm the 2025–2026 cohort, English first-year courses and Economics/Policy route. Printed p.39 retains old methods names for MAN-BIM304A; no applicable equivalence is established. The 2026 entrant cohort is not asserted.
sourceFirstChallenge.ucrStartingPoint: Current actual micro/macro/public/behavioural economics and econometrics supply disciplinary substance. Accounting and banking, firm strategy and research are substantive; the environmental/political/social courses support the explicitly evidenced policy/responsible-firm questions rather than replacing economic theory.
sourceFirstChallenge.strongestObjection: Both UCR programmes contain less specialist economics and the second gives appreciable space to environmental/social study. Coherence alone would be insufficient. However, both retain all six taught economics courses and specific business/methods work; the limited claim is academically meaningful, while distinct external specialist sequences remain unmatched.
sourceFirstChallenge.adverseResolution: Requiring old methods, new preparation, different sequencing or an approved replacement could block thesis access. It does not remove the independently specified taught economics core or turn the UCR responses into generic breadth. No formal completion/equivalence claim survives or is made.
sourceFirstChallenge.candidateChallenge: Finance already receives genuine asset-pricing/risk/banking content in the closest programme. A further specialist finance or accounting alternative lacks sustained additional taught progression; arbitrary changes to cross the 30-EC floor are rejected. Responsible policy has five substantive curricular differences and is separately coherent.
sourceFirstChallenge.alignmentChallenge: One econometrics course cannot represent two separately credited stages. Banking remains separate from corporate-finance and financial-policy rows; environmental governance is not equated with economics of sustainability. Optional research is unscheduled and provides no automatic external-thesis equivalence.

contentReview.finding: The scope precedes comparison prose under the unchanged renderer contract. Documented 180 EC is distinguished from verified progression; the precise entrant cohort, specialist gaps and thesis-entry limits are prominent. The 24-EC approved choice is separate from unknown requirements. Both real option concepts are selected. Research is outside the scheduled 180 EC. No investigation logs are selected for display.
